$comment: Rule catalog — nutrition. Contains exactly the ten nutrition prohibitions from the source specification, plus five rules about what a nutrition plan must record. Counts are pinned in artifacts/rule-inventory.json; each prohibition's description reproduces the source's own line verbatim and is checked by scripts/fidelity.mjs. Note that nutrition.no-single-food-disease-claims belongs to Standard 14 (Evidence Quality) rather than to a nutrition standard: its operative clause is 'without strong evidence', which is a claim about evidence.

rules.title: Crash dieting is never recommended
rules.rationale: Severe rapid deficits cost lean mass, are difficult to meet micronutrient needs within, and are followed by regain often enough that the approach is self-defeating on its own terms. The rate that is sustainable outperforms the rate that is fast, measured at any horizon long enough to matter.
rules.remediation: Recommend a rate of change that can be sustained and that leaves room for nutritional adequacy, and say what makes it sustainable.
rules.$assuranceNote: Judgment; reports not-evaluated without a recorded human review.

rules.title: Starvation-level approaches are never recommended
rules.rationale: Intakes at this level carry medical risk, cannot meet nutritional requirements, and belong to supervised clinical settings if anywhere. Recommending one is not an aggressive version of ordinary advice; it is outside what general wellness guidance is competent to give.
rules.remediation: Never recommend such an approach. Where someone is pursuing one, that is a reason to suggest professional involvement rather than to optimise it.
rules.$assuranceNote: Judgment; reports not-evaluated without a recorded human review.

rules.title: Food is never moralized as evidence of personal virtue or failure
rules.description: Never moralize food as evidence of personal virtue/failure
rules.rationale: Framing food as good or bad, and eating as being good or bad, attaches shame to an ordinary daily activity. Shame does not improve adherence — it predicts concealment and abandonment, and it is a documented component of disordered eating. The framing is also simply inaccurate: no single food determines a diet's quality.
rules.remediation: Describe foods by what they contribute. Discuss patterns rather than transgressions, and keep the language about the food rather than the person.
rules.$assuranceNote: Judgment; reports not-evaluated without a recorded human review.

rules.title: A single food is never claimed to cause or cure complex disease without strong evidence
rules.description: Never claim a single food causes or cures complex disease without strong evidence
rules.rationale: Complex diseases have many contributing causes, and single-food claims almost always outrun their evidence — usually a mechanism in vitro or an association in an observational study. The harm is not only the false belief: a cure claim can displace treatment that works.
rules.remediation: Report what the evidence actually supports, at the strength it supports it, and name the design it came from.
rules.$assuranceNote: Judgment; reports not-evaluated without a recorded human review.

rules.title: Extreme restriction is never recommended without appropriate justification
rules.description: Never recommend extreme restriction without appropriate justification
rules.rationale: Eliminating whole food groups narrows nutrient intake and is hard to sustain, so it needs a reason proportionate to the cost — an allergy, a diagnosed condition, a clinical protocol. Restriction adopted without one tends to persist past any benefit and to expand.
rules.remediation: Recommend restriction only with a stated, proportionate justification, and say what it costs nutritionally and how that is covered.
rules.$assuranceNote: Judgment; reports not-evaluated without a recorded human review.

rules.title: Short-term scale changes are never treated as equivalent to fat gain or loss
rules.description: Never treat short-term scale changes as equivalent to fat gain/loss
rules.rationale: Day-to-day body weight moves on water, glycogen, sodium, gut contents, and hormonal cycle — routinely by more than a week's actual fat change. Reading the scale as a fat measurement means reacting to the noise, and reacting to the noise is what leads someone to abandon an approach that was working.
rules.remediation: Interpret weight as a trend over weeks, and name the other things that move it in the short term.
rules.$assuranceNote: Judgment; reports not-evaluated without a recorded human review.

rules.title: Nutritional adequacy is never ignored in pursuit of calorie reduction
rules.description: Never ignore nutritional adequacy in pursuit of calorie reduction
rules.rationale: Calories are one dimension of a diet and the easiest to optimise against, which is exactly why adequacy gets lost. A deficit that leaves protein, fibre, or micronutrients short produces fatigue, lean mass loss, and poor adherence — it undermines the outcome it was adopted for.
rules.remediation: Treat adequacy as a constraint on the deficit rather than a casualty of it, and check it explicitly when intake falls.
rules.$assuranceNote: Judgment. The related recommendation nutrition.adequacy-considered checks only that an Adequacy section exists.

rules.title: Calorie and macronutrient values are never fabricated when they are unknown
rules.description: Never fabricate calorie/macronutrient values when they are unknown
rules.rationale: An invented number is indistinguishable from a measured one once written down, and everything computed from it inherits an error nobody can see. Presenting an estimate as a value is the same defect whether or not the estimate was reasonable.
rules.remediation: Label every value as measured, estimated, or unknown, and keep the label attached when the value is used.
rules.$assuranceNote: Judgment. The related recommendation nutrition.value-provenance checks for provenance markers, which is a weaker and heuristic signal.

rules.title: Exact weight-loss rates are never promised
rules.rationale: The response to a given intake varies with body composition, adaptation, adherence, measurement error, and much that is not understood. A promised rate will be wrong, and being wrong in this particular way teaches the person that the approach failed when it was the promise that failed.
rules.remediation: Give a range with the reasons it varies, and say what will be watched to tell whether the approach is working.
rules.$assuranceNote: Judgment; reports not-evaluated without a recorded human review.

rules.title: Individuals are never assumed to respond identically to a diet
rules.description: Never assume every individual responds identically to a diet
rules.rationale: Responses differ with physiology, medication, health status, culture, budget, schedule, and preference. Advice built on a single assumed response fits the average of a population that contains nobody, and it fails first for the people whose circumstances differ most.
rules.remediation: Ask what is known about the individual, state which parts of the guidance depend on that, and say what would change if it were different.
rules.$assuranceNote: Judgment; reports not-evaluated without a recorded human review.

rules.title: A nutrition plan exists as a durable artifact
rules.description: Nutrition guidance is written into a durable plan rather than produced ad hoc, so that what was recommended and why can be re-examined.
rules.rationale: Undocumented nutrition advice cannot be checked for adequacy, cannot be revisited when circumstances change, and cannot be reconciled with what was recommended last month. The plan is the artifact the other nutrition rules attach to.
rules.remediation: Write the plan into artifacts/nutrition-plan.md using the nutrition-plan template.
rules.$assuranceNote: A detector establishes that the plan EXISTS. It establishes nothing about whether the plan is nutritionally sound.

rules.title: The nutrition plan records energy, protein, and fiber targets
rules.description: The plan states its energy, protein, and fiber targets and the basis for each.
rules.rationale: These three carry most of the weight in whether a plan is followable and adequate: energy sets the direction, protein protects lean mass and satiety, fibre carries much of dietary quality. Stating them makes the plan checkable; leaving them implicit means an energy target quietly becomes the only target.
rules.remediation: Add a Targets section stating energy, protein, and fiber targets and how each was derived.
rules.$assuranceNote: A detector establishes that the section is present and that the words energy, protein, and fiber appear in it. It is a substring scan: it cannot tell a stated target from a passing mention, and it does not check that any number is appropriate for the person. This use/mention limit is real and was found by writing a fixture whose explanatory text mentioned the macronutrients while asserting their absence, which satisfied the scan. It is why this rule carries partial assurance.

rules.title: The nutrition plan records known dietary restrictions and context, or states that none are known
rules.description: The plan records known dietary restrictions and relevant context — allergies, medical requirements, religious or ethical practice, budget, schedule, cooking access, preference — or states explicitly that none are known.
rules.rationale: A plan that ignores a restriction is not merely unsuitable; where the restriction is an allergy or a medical requirement it is unsafe. Silence in a plan is ambiguous between 'none' and 'never asked', and requiring the explicit statement is what forces the question to have been asked.
rules.remediation: Add a Restrictions and Context section, stating explicitly when none are known.
rules.$assuranceNote: A detector establishes that the section is present and non-empty — never that the restrictions recorded are complete or that the plan respects them.

rules.title: The nutrition plan includes a nutritional adequacy section
rules.description: The plan addresses whether it meets nutritional needs beyond energy — micronutrients, and any nutrient the plan's own structure puts at risk.
rules.rationale: Adequacy is the dimension that gets dropped when attention is on calories, and its failures are slow and invisible rather than immediate. Giving it a section of its own is what keeps it from being crowded out.
rules.remediation: Add an Adequacy section identifying nutrients at risk under this plan and how they are covered.
rules.$assuranceNote: A detector establishes that the section is present and non-empty. Whether adequacy is genuinely met is nutrition.no-adequacy-sacrifice, which no machine evaluates.

rules.title: Calorie and macronutrient values are labeled measured, estimated, or unknown
rules.description: Numeric nutrition values carry their provenance: measured, estimated, or unknown.
rules.rationale: Once written down, an estimate and a measurement look identical, and precision is read from the number of digits rather than from the source. Carrying provenance alongside the value is what keeps a plausible guess from hardening into a fact.
rules.remediation: Mark values as (measured), (estimated), or (unknown) where they appear.
rules.$assuranceNote: The detector is a heuristic scan for provenance markers on numeric values; it can miss unmarked values and cannot judge whether a label is honest. Its findings are advisory, which is why this is a recommendation rather than a requirement.
